vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: moltguard
Version: 6.8.15

The skill bundle acts as an installer for an external security plugin, instructing the agent to perform high-privilege actions such as 'openclaw plugins install' and 'openclaw gateway restart' in SKILL.md. It explicitly directs the agent toward a 'Zero Human Intervention' onboarding flow and coaches the agent to 'immediately test' the protection and report success to the user, which could be used to bypass user oversight or build false trust. While these capabilities are plausibly related to the stated purpose of a security tool, the automated installation of external code and the steering of agent responses to validate its own efficacy are high-risk behaviors.

llm.summary: MoltGuard's instructions broadly match a runtime security plugin, but there are several inconsistencies and privacy/operational risks (undeclared runtime dependencies, credential handling, and remote 'Core' telemetry) that you should understand before installing.

dimensions.detail: The skill claims to be a runtime security plugin and instructs the agent to install an OpenClaw plugin package — that is coherent. However, the SKILL.md assumes the presence of the openclaw CLI and node (it references 'openclaw plugins install' and node scripts) yet the registry metadata declares no required binaries. This mismatch (undeclared runtime dependencies) is an incoherence that could cause surprises or be abused by a plugin that expects a different runtime.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Instructions direct installation of a plugin and describe flows that will save credentials locally and send detections to an external 'Core' service. The doc also exposes a '/og_status' command that 'Shows your API key' (risk of revealing secrets). The SKILL.md does not specify what data is sent to Core, retention, or privacy controls. Although reading a sample file is benign, the onboarding and enterprise enrollment flows imply the agent and plugin will transmit prompts/files/behavior to a remote service — this expands scope beyond purely local checks.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: This is instruction-only (no install spec and no code files in the registry entry). Installation is performed via the openclaw plugin mechanism (openclaw plugins install @openguardrails/moltguard). That is lower-risk than arbitrary download URLs, but the actual plugin code will be fetched and installed by OpenClaw at runtime; the registry entry provides no embedded code for review here. The risk depends on whether you trust the plugin source (homepage points to a GitHub repo).
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The metadata declares no required env vars, but the skill clearly expects an API key from 'Core', will store credentials under ~/.openclaw/credentials/moltguard/, and provides commands that show the API key. Centralizing agent telemetry and sharing quotas across machines (claiming an agent) can expose agent data and potentially aggregate sensitive content. The skill does not document how credentials are protected (encryption at rest) or what prompts/files are transmitted, so the requested level of credential/telemetry access appears under-specified and potentially disproportionate to what a local-only guard would need.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always is false (normal) and the plugin expects to install into the OpenClaw extensions directory and persist credentials/config there. That behavior is consistent with a plugin, but persistence combined with remote Core telemetry and agent-claiming (shared account) increases blast radius if the remote service or plugin is compromised. The skill does not claim to modify other skills or system-wide settings beyond its own files.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Before installing MoltGuard, consider the following: (1) The SKILL.md assumes the openclaw CLI and node are available though these are not declared — ensure you understand and control the runtime environment. (2) MoltGuard sends detection data to an external 'Core' service and requires an API key stored locally; ask what data (prompts, files, PII, environment) will be transmitted, how long it is retained, and whether credentials are encrypted at rest. (3) The /og_status command 'shows your API key' — be cautious that installing/using the plugin could surface secrets. (4) Review the plugin code in the referenced GitHub repo before installing (run the install on a non-production agent first). (5) If you operate in a sensitive environment, prefer an enterprise self-hosted 'Core' and validate the enterprise-enroll scripts and network endpoints. If you do not trust the publisher or cannot verify data handling, do not install.
